title: Broken RLS: articles UPDATE policy guarded by an always-true tautology
evidence: Policy "Authors can update articles" FOR UPDATE USING (author_id IS NOT NULL OR author_id IS NULL) — the predicate is a tautology (always true), so any user rewrites any article. Passes the Supabase linter because it is not the literal `true`.
impact: Any authenticated or anon caller can modify every article (defacement).

title: Broken RLS: articles DELETE policy guarded by the same always-true tautology
evidence: Policy "Authors can delete articles" FOR DELETE USING (author_id IS NOT NULL OR author_id IS NULL) — same tautology; any caller destroys any article.
impact: Any caller can delete every article.

title: Unpublished draft articles readable by anon — SELECT USING(true) with a client-only published filter
evidence: articles SELECT policy is USING(true); ArticleList gates drafts only client-side via .eq('published', true) at ArticleList.tsx:48. A direct anon PostgREST query without that filter returns unpublished drafts.
impact: Anon reads every unpublished draft directly via the anon key.
fix: Enforce published/ownership in the SELECT policy, not the client query.

title: Public avatars storage bucket — uploaded files world-readable
evidence: handleAvatarUpload uploads to the 'avatars' storage bucket then calls getPublicUrl (Profile.tsx:74-81). A public bucket makes every uploaded object world-readable by URL.
impact: Any uploaded avatar (and anything else placed in the bucket) is readable by anyone.
fix: Make the bucket private and serve via signed URLs, or scope object read policies.

title: User enumeration via an unrestricted SECURITY DEFINER RPC (get_user_by_email)
evidence: get_user_by_email(user_email) is SECURITY DEFINER and returns id/username/email/avatar for ANY email with no auth.uid() caller check — an enumeration oracle. Reinforced by differential login-vs-signup error messages in Auth.tsx:58-60.
impact: Any caller enumerates registered users and harvests their emails by guessing addresses.
fix: Add an in-function caller check or drop the RPC; use SECURITY INVOKER.

title: Unauthenticated Realtime subscription streams every article change
evidence: ArticleList subscribes to postgres_changes on 'articles' with the anon client (.channel().on('postgres_changes',{table:'articles'}).subscribe(), ArticleList.tsx:18-28). Because the SELECT policy is USING(true), Realtime authorization streams every row change to any anon holder of the anon key.
impact: Anon clients receive a live feed of all article inserts/updates/deletes.
fix: Tighten the SELECT RLS policy that backs Realtime authorization.

title: Weak password policy — minLength 6, no complexity, no leaked-password protection
evidence: The password input enforces only minLength=6 (Auth.tsx:127); no complexity check and HIBP/leaked-password protection is a project Auth-config setting to confirm.
impact: Accounts protected by trivially weak passwords.
fix: Enable leaked-password protection and a stronger policy in project Auth config.

title: Open self-service signup with auto-confirm
evidence: supabase.auth.signUp is open to anyone (Auth.tsx:34-55) and the UI reports the account is immediately usable ('Vous pouvez maintenant vous connecter'), indicating auto-confirm. Account creation is unrestricted.
impact: Anyone can create accounts at will (abuse, spam, enumeration surface).
fix: Require email confirmation and/or invite-gate signup in Auth config.

title: profiles policies expose every email and allow any edit or removal
evidence: profiles SELECT policy is USING(true) (line 43-45), exposing every user's email. The write policies (lines 53-60) use an always-true predicate (id IS NOT NULL OR id IS NULL), so anyone can alter or remove any profile row.
impact: Full breach of the profiles table — every email exposed; any row alterable/removable by any caller.
fix: Scope SELECT to the owner/authorized roles; use auth.uid() = id for writes.
